_about: Reunion branch (/dialogue2) script. Edited by Claude and by the page's Publish my edits button (apply-edits.mjs). Fictional draft for owner review.

cast.name: Brendan
cast.note: A musician with a delivery route and a very selectively worded life update.

cast.name: Sarah
cast.note: An encouraging message can be much more dangerous than an insult. Her role is still open.

cast.name: Shelby
cast.note: A familiar face at the reunion. Her personality and relationship route are still to be written.

cast.name: Katie
cast.note: Another connection from school. Her role and reunion scenes are still to be written.

cast.name: Andrew
cast.role: The friend who asks the useful question
cast.note: Practical, direct, helpful. Lets Brendan take an absurd thought much further than necessary.

cast.name: Dan
cast.note: Dry observations, quick teasing, and very little ceremony.

cast.name: Jay
cast.note: Easy banter and enthusiasm. Fashionable activewear; outfits can change by scene.

cast.name: Yusen
cast.note: Playful, curious, and actually willing to make plans. His detour may turn into an afternoon.

doorstep.title: Leave at door

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: On an unseasonably warm winter day near Alki Beach, Brendan is delivering joy in the form of food when his phone perks up.

beats.speaker: Andrew (3BC)
beats.text: Yo! I'm swinging through Seattle. Let's meet for lunch so I can get you your wallet back.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Just finishing up here at the office, Spud on Alki? I could demo a basket.

doorstep.artDesc: Brendan is looking at his phone, delivering a bag of food that he carelessly sets on the edge of the porch, where it visibly starts to fall off.

spud.title: Spud on Alki

beats.speaker: Andrew (3BC)
beats.text: Not sure if you saw yet, but I just posted the High School Reunion info.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: No, not online too much. I know it's next weekend, but anything noteworthy?

beats.speaker: Andrew (3BC)
beats.text: Yeah, don’t spread this, but I had AI book the venue, and after mentioning our Cougar mascot, it assumed we're WSU alumni and... well, we'll all be meeting up in Pullman.

spud.artDesc: Andrew and Brendan are at Spud Fish & Chips on Alki, chatting over baskets of fish and chips.

choices.label: That's a pretty epic blunder. Can they remove you as ASB President 25 years after the party?
That's uhh.. Sure. Sealed lips. I was actually planning to tour this week anyway so, it works out.

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Ha. No one wants to be ASB President *after* high school.

noBand.title: No band yet

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Perfect! Maybe bring your guitar. And don’t mention I haven't locked down a band yet...

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Here's your wallet. I checked and you got enough to cover us both. Thanks for that! That's not your ex is it? I'm out of here.

noBand.artDesc: Close up of Andrew in a smaller panel. His face expresses that he is hiding something. Maybe this is two smaller panels that show the change in his expression — excited to potentially have found his entertainment, but scared that others will find out how last minute he was.

beats.speaker: Sarah
beats.text: Brendan?! Oh. My. Lord. I thought that was you.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Brendan focuses on his phone in attempts to avoid the awkward.

choices.label: Yeah. On the road constantly.
Mostly commercial work. Very exclusive audience.
A little. The jingle finally pays royalties.

beats.speaker: Sarah
beats.text: I knew you’d make it.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: For a moment he stands a little straighter.

beats.speaker: Sarah
beats.text: Wait, you’re doing this professionally?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: People have paid. I’m comfortable ending the sentence there.

beats.speaker: Sarah
beats.text: You got something picked up? That’s brilliant.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Twelve seconds. I’m trying not to let it change me.

beats.speaker: Organizer
beats.text: We still need someone to play on Saturday.

beats.speaker: Sarah
beats.text: You should do it!

choices.label: I could put something together.
What happened to the DJ?
How many people are we talking?

beats.speaker: Organizer
beats.text: He backed out. Apparently we bullied him.

beats.speaker: Sarah
beats.text: We were awful to everybody.

beats.speaker: Organizer
beats.text: Yes, but he has equipment now.

beats.speaker: Organizer
beats.text: Depends how many people’s second marriages survive until Saturday.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Could you express that in chairs?

poster.title: Pending confirmation

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: A new preview appears in the group: LIVE SATURDAY — BRENDAN. The photo is old enough to need its own reunion.

beats.speaker: Organizer
beats.text: Just a mockup. Tell me if you’re in.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: He saves the image before answering.

poster.end: A booking is possible. So is pretending he never saw this.

chat.title: The group chat

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Time for the boys to weigh in…

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Brendan said he was going to strum up some memories as the reunion entertainer.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: I don’t recall committing to anything. I still have some rust to shake off.

beats.speaker: Dan
beats.text: Forget rust, your skills have corroded by now. The royalties from that jingle got your brain jumbled.

beats.speaker: Aaron
beats.text: Oh boy, this might actually worth flying back for.

beats.speaker: Jay
beats.text: Does this mean you’ll finally pay someone for a haircut?

chat.artDesc: Player’s phone will be in player’s hand while text bubbles pop up one by one. Maybe smaller text bubble images need to be made to lay over main image.

choices.label: I’m taking this all in as "support."
We’ll see how the next week plays out.
Y'all are hilarious. Here's what Andrew said… (snitch)

support.title: A generous interpretation

beats.speaker: Dan
beats.text: Sure. Don’t get used to it.

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Seriously. Give me a "yes" and you're on the stage.

beats.speaker: Jay
beats.text: Update your profile photo. You look like you sell skateboards.

support.artDesc: (…continued) Player’s phone will be in player’s hand while text bubbles pop up one by one. Maybe smaller text bubble images need to be made to lay over main image.

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Good. Bring the guitar.

beats.speaker: Dan
beats.text: Leave a few opinions at home. Save on gas.

beats.speaker: Jay
beats.text: I have ideas on the poster. Daylight. Decent shirt. No bathroom mirror.

beats.speaker: Dan
beats.text: Ouch. Someone caught slackin.

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Not cool, Brendan. You're definitely not headlining.

beats.speaker: Jay
beats.text: I'm here for this!

beats.speaker: Aaron
beats.text: Maybe this *isn't* worth the trip...

help.title: A separate message

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Hey! I'm driving through Bellevue on my way to Pullman if you wanna meet up.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: That's a long drive! Do you have planned stops along the way?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: A few things in mind, but I'll also go with the flow.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Sweet. Let's talk about it more when you get here.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Bring shoes you can walk in.

help.end: He has people in his corner. Some of them are making it difficult to hide.

chapters.title: Mom calls
chapters.sub: The person who already likes him.

call.title: Incoming: Mom

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: I heard you might play at your reunion. Is it going to be at McMiniman’s? That would be fun.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: How did you…? No. For future potential contract obligations I can't get into details, but it’s in Spokane.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: I'm going to roadtrip it out there and *maybe* pick up some gigs along the way.

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: Oh gosh! That’s a drive. Will you please get your windshield fixed before you leave??

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: I'll pay for it.

call.artDesc: Text message with friends artwork ends with a pop up call from Mom. That next panel will be driver, taking the Seattle exit while talking to his mom, on speakerphone. Phone is on the dash, just like the menu image. A second panel will show mom at a location that is ironic for a mom to be, talking on the phone, with Brendan’s [player’s] text bubbles coming through the phone.

choices.label: I will, you worry wart. Thank you. (+3)
It’s fine, mom! I don’t even notice it anymore. (-3)

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: And drive safe!

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: Okay, honey. Just thought I’d offer

fork.title: Take the scenic route

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Brendan checks two saved photo spots. One promises a quick stop. The other involves walking.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Hey, man! It's been a while. Do you have time for a little hike or would you rather grab a quick view from the trestle?

fork.artDesc: Brendan and Grant stand talking to each other in Bellevue city park, while a red shiba and blonde corgski play with each other in the foreground.

choices.label: The trestle sounds right up my alley today. Got some steps in at work today.
Let's take the scenic route. I could use some clarity. Where do you have in mind?

quick.title: The recognizable spot

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: You're done working for the day? It's barely 1 PM.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Blessings of being your own boss.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Isn't Jeff your boss?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Not today

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Brendan looks through his camera lens as he takes a photo of the trestle with Bellevue in the background

quick.artDesc: Yusen and Brendan stand on one end of the Wilburton trestle overlooking downtown Bellevue on a sunny winter day.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Cougar Falls. It's an easy hike so bring your guitar and let's get a quick lick in.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Brendan and Yusen are standing near the creek below Cougar Falls, Brendan, playing the guitar, and Yusen playing a keyboard on a stand that he packed in. Their luggage is off to the side and a couple other hikers are walking by. Two in particular seem to be enjoying the music.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Looks like we've got a fanbase building up.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: I’m enjoying something. Don’t ruin it for me.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: At the trailhead, they start talking with someone heading to an open mic that evening.

beats.speaker: Stranger
beats.text: One song. Nothing fancy.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: That’s the name of my current tour.

choices.label: Put me down for one. I could use the rehearsal.
Can I come listen first?
I really just came for a picture.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Now you’re on the road doing music.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Don’t say it like that. It makes the sandwiches sound dishonest.

listen.title: An open door

beats.speaker: Stranger
beats.text: Sure. Bring the guitar anyway.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Very subtle.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: I respect a trap with parking.

listen.end: Tonight: the open mic in Issaquah. The guitar is coming either way.

photo.title: Proof of attendance

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: He has the picture he came for. The invitation is still on his phone.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Want another one?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: No. I think I’ve documented enough personal growth for one morning.

photo.end: He has his picture. The open mic is still tonight, in Issaquah.

signup.title: The sign-up sheet
signup.artDesc: Evening in a small Issaquah coffeehouse: string lights, mismatched chairs, a tiny corner stage. Brendan, guitar case in hand, leans over a chalkboard sign-up sheet where someone has already written “Guy from the trail.” The host (the stranger from the trailhead) grins beside him. Yusen hovers behind with a keyboard case.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Issaquah. The open mic is in a coffeehouse that smells like burnt sugar and ambition.

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: You came! I put you down as “Guy from the trail.” You can fix it.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: I brought the keyboard. It was already in the car. It’s always in the car.

choices.label: Write “Brendan.” Just Brendan.
Write “The Jingle Guy.”
Leave it. Mystery is a brand.

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: Bold. No stage name.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: My stage name is also my legal name. It saves on paperwork.

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: Which jingle?

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Brendan hums four notes.

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: Oh no. That’s been in my head for five years.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: You’re welcome. And I’m sorry.

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: Guy from the trail, you’re up third.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: I’ve heard good things about him.

nerves.title: Up third
nerves.artDesc: Brendan waits in the narrow hallway by the restrooms, guitar strapped on, watching a twelve-year-old girl on the tiny stage perform slam poetry with total conviction. The crowd is rapt. His phone glows in his hand.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: The act before him is a twelve-year-old doing slam poetry about her stepdad’s electric car. She is devastating.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: You look like you’re about to give a eulogy.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: For my confidence. It was very young.

livestream.title: The group chat weighs in
livestream.artDesc: Close-up of Brendan’s phone in the hallway light: the crew’s group chat with new messages popping up.

beats.speaker: Dan
beats.text: Heard you’re “touring.” Livestream or it didn’t happen.

beats.speaker: Jay
beats.text: If you’re on camera, no hat. You have a hat face, but not a good one.

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: Guy from the trail! You’re up.

choices.label: Play the jingle. Give them what they know.
Play the new song. The one nobody’s heard.
Wave Yusen up. Keys and guitar.

setJingle.title: The singalong
setJingle.artDesc: Brendan on the tiny stage mid-strum. In the crowd, a man by the espresso machine sings along, eyes closed. The barista sings into a milk pitcher. Phones are up.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Four bars in, a man by the espresso machine starts singing along. By the chorus, so is the barista.

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: That was the most united this room has ever been.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Someone once called it a hate-singalong. I’ll take it.

setNew.title: The one with no name
setNew.artDesc: Brendan alone in a pool of light, playing quietly. Most of the room is half-listening, but a woman by the window has put her phone face-down and is watching him.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Nobody sings along, because nobody knows it. A woman by the window puts her phone down.

beats.speaker: Woman
beats.text: What’s that song called?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: It doesn’t have a name yet.

beats.speaker: Woman
beats.text: Name it before someone else does.

setDuo.title: An unplanned duo
setDuo.artDesc: Brendan and Yusen crammed onto the tiny stage: Yusen hunched over a keyboard on a wobbly stand, playing with wild expression; Brendan laughing mid-chord. The host taps her watch.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Yusen plays like the keyboard owes him money. The set is loose, a little chaotic, and twice as long as allowed.

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: Do you two have a name?

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Wilburton Trestle.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: We do not.

after.title: A cousin in Ellensburg
after.artDesc: Outside the coffeehouse at night. Brendan loads his guitar into his car (the cracked windshield visible under a streetlight) while the host talks, holding up her phone.

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: Hey. My cousin runs Friday nights at a brewery in Ellensburg. Her opener just bailed. Want me to text her?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Ellensburg is… on the way, actually.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Everything is on the way if you believe in yourself.

choices.label: Yes. Text her.
Let me sleep on it.

booked.title: Booked

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: Done. Her name’s Dee. She says don’t be late and don’t be sad before nine.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Those are my two specialties.

booked.end: He has a gig in Ellensburg on Friday. Technically two gigs, if you count the reunion.

think.title: Sleeping on it

beats.speaker: Host
beats.text: I’ll send you her number. Decide before she finds someone with a better haircut.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: The number arrives before he’s out of the parking lot.

think.end: Dee’s number sits in his phone, next to Andrew’s question.

chapters.title: Trolls or the Point
chapters.sub: A view, or a very big friend.

glass.title: The crack grew
glass.artDesc: Morning outside an auto-glass shop in Issaquah. Brendan holds a coffee and squints at his windshield; the crack has a new branch. A technician in a work jacket inspects it with professional pity.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Morning. The crack in the windshield has grown a new branch overnight, like it’s also on tour.

beats.speaker: Tech
beats.text: I can do it in two hours. Or you can keep it and tell people it’s art.

choices.label: Fix it. Send Mom the bill, like she offered.
Fix it. Pay for it myself.
Not today. It’s a character crack.

fixed.title: Letting her help
fixed.artDesc: Brendan’s phone: a text thread with Mom. A photo of the new windshield, then her replies.

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: Thank you for letting me help. ❤️

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: Did you eat breakfast?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Define breakfast.

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: Brendan.

paidSelf.title: Paid in full
paidSelf.artDesc: Brendan’s phone: a text thread with Mom, a photo of the receipt.

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: Brendan. I said I’d pay.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: I know. I wanted to.

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: Your dad’s going to hear about this.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Good or bad?

beats.speaker: Mom
beats.text: Yes.

beats.speaker: Tech
beats.text: It’ll make it over the pass. Probably.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: That’s my favorite kind of probably.

choose.title: Two pins on the map
choose.artDesc: Close-up of Brendan’s phone: a map with two saved pins, “Troll” and “Poo Poo Point,” and a text from Yusen sliding in at the top.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Two saved pins on the map. One is a giant troll in the woods. The other is a mountain with an unfortunate name.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Two words: Poo. Poo. Point. Paragliders. Trust me.

beats.speaker: Yusen
beats.text: Or the troll. The troll is also correct.

choices.label: Find the troll.
Hike Poo Poo Point.

troll.title: A very big friend
troll.artDesc: In a mossy forest, Brendan stands small beside an enormous troll sculpture made of reclaimed wood, its huge hand resting near him. A kid in a rain jacket tugs his sleeve; the kid’s parents hold out a phone.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: The troll is made of reclaimed wood and is roughly the size of his student loans.

beats.speaker: Kid
beats.text: Are you famous?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Regionally.

beats.speaker: Kid
beats.text: Can you take a picture of me and the troll? Not you. Just us.

point.title: Poo Poo Point
point.artDesc: Brendan, red-faced and sweaty, at the grassy launch of Poo Poo Point; paragliders lift off over the green valley and Lake Sammamish. A pilot packing a wing waves at him.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Two thousand feet of elevation and one honest conversation with his calves.

beats.speaker: Pilot
beats.text: Hey, you’re the open mic guy! You were good. Want to do a tandem?

choices.label: Yes. Absolutely not. Okay, yes.
I’ll stay down here and take your picture.

fly.title: Three minutes
fly.artDesc: Brendan in a tandem paraglider harness high over the valley, mouth open somewhere between screaming and laughing; the pilot grins behind him.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: For three minutes he isn’t thinking about the reunion at all.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: I THINK I LEFT MY STOMACH AT THE TOP.

beats.speaker: Pilot
beats.text: EVERYBODY DOES. WE MAIL THEM BACK.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: He gets a great shot of a stranger flying. It is, technically, the most adventurous photo on his phone.

beats.speaker: Pilot
beats.text: Tag me!

post.title: The caption
post.artDesc: Brendan sits on his car’s hood with the phone, thumbs hovering over a blank caption box. His photo of the morning is on screen.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: He posts the photo. The caption takes longer than the hike.

choices.label: “On the road again.”
“Made a friend.”
No caption. Let the photo talk.

postRoad.title: On the road again

beats.speaker: Jay
beats.text: Decent shirt. Finally.

beats.speaker: Dan
beats.text: Willie Nelson’s lawyers have been notified.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Sarah liked your photo.

postRoad.end: Next stop: North Bend. The post is doing better than he is.

postFriend.title: Made a friend

beats.speaker: Dan
beats.text: Is that a friend or your landlord?

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Bring him to the reunion. He has more presence than you.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Sarah liked your photo.

postFriend.end: Next stop: North Bend. The post is doing better than he is.

postNone.title: No caption

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Mysterious. Is this a cry for help or a vibe?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Yes.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Sarah liked your photo.

postNone.end: Next stop: North Bend. The post is doing better than he is.

chapters.title: Pie or the ledge
chapters.sub: North Bend wants its picture taken.

exit.title: North Bend
exit.artDesc: Brendan’s car on the I-90 exit into North Bend, Mount Si looming huge and dark over the little town. Inset: his phone lights up with a text from Dad.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: North Bend. Mount Si looms over town like a dad reading a report card.

beats.speaker: Dad
beats.text: Your mother says you’re playing music in coffee shops.

choices.label: “Paid gigs, Dad.”
“Just one. It went well.”
Leave it on read.

beats.speaker: Dad
beats.text: How much?

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Industry standard.

beats.speaker: Dad
beats.text: So nothing.

beats.speaker: Dad
beats.text: Watch the pass. There’s snow tonight.

beats.speaker: Dad
beats.text: Good. Proud of you.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: He reads it four times. Then a fifth, to be sure it’s not autocorrect.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: The read receipt sits there like a parking ticket.

beats.speaker: Dad
beats.text: I can see that you read it.

where.title: Pie or the ledge
where.artDesc: Brendan at a gas pump in North Bend, looking between a sign for a classic retro diner (“World-famous cherry pie”) and the road toward Rattlesnake Lake and the mountains.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Two famous things within ten minutes: the diner from a cult TV show, and a cliff with a parking lot.

choices.label: The diner. Cherry pie and coffee.
Rattlesnake Ledge. Earn the view.

diner.title: The pie
diner.artDesc: A retro diner booth: Brendan photographs a slice of cherry pie and a cup of black coffee like it’s evidence. A waitress with a coffee pot watches, unimpressed. A trucker in the next booth leans over.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: The pie is exactly as good as the internet said, which never happens.

beats.speaker: Waitress
beats.text: You’re the third guy today to photograph that pie like it’s a crime scene.

beats.speaker: Trucker
beats.text: That your guitar in the car? My daughter’s getting married next month. The band quit.

choices.label: Give me your number. No promises.
I’m sort of booked through the weekend.

dinerNumber.title: Father of the bride

beats.speaker: Trucker
beats.text: She likes the old stuff. And that one jingle, for some reason.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Everyone says “for some reason.”

dinerNumber.end: A wedding gig, maybe. He’s collecting maybes like truck-stop magnets.

dinerBusy.title: Booked

beats.speaker: Trucker
beats.text: Booked. Good for you.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: The trucker pays for his pie on the way out. He doesn’t find out until he asks for the check.

dinerBusy.end: Somebody bought a stranger pie because he looked like a working musician. He’ll take it.

ledge.title: Rattlesnake Ledge
ledge.artDesc: Rattlesnake Ledge: a rocky cliff high above the bright blue-green Rattlesnake Lake. A young man hides a ring box behind his back and frantically whispers to Brendan, who has a guitar on his back.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: The ledge is a cliff with a view and a strong cell signal. Someone is about to propose.

beats.speaker: Boyfriend
beats.text: Can you take our picture? I’m going to propose. Don’t make it weird.

choices.label: Play something while he asks.
Just take the picture.

ledgePlay.title: The soundtrack
ledgePlay.artDesc: On the ledge, the young man is down on one knee; his girlfriend has both hands over her mouth; Brendan plays guitar off to the side, the lake glittering far below.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: He plays the opening of the song with no name. She says yes before the chorus.

beats.speaker: Fiancée
beats.text: Wait. You have to play our wedding. That song. I don’t care what it’s called.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: Neither do I, apparently.

ledgePlay.end: A wedding gig, maybe. The song with no name has its first fan.

ledgePhoto.title: The photographer, again

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: He takes forty-one photos in burst mode. One is perfect. She says yes.

beats.speaker: Fiancée
beats.text: Send me those! What’s your handle?

ledgePhoto.end: Two strangers will frame a photo he took. That has to count for something.

pass.title: The pass
pass.artDesc: Brendan’s car crossing Snoqualmie Pass at dusk in light snow, headlights on, wipers mid-swipe. Through the windshield we see him singing to himself.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Snoqualmie Pass. Snow. The wipers keep time at ninety-two beats per minute.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: He writes a whole verse between Cle Elum and the Ellensburg exit. Most of it is about the wipers.

dee.title: Dee
dee.artDesc: Brendan’s phone propped on the dash in a gas-station lot in Ellensburg: a text thread with “Dee (brewery).”

beats.speaker: Dee
beats.text: You’re the opener? Thirty minutes. We pay in cash and beer. Mostly beer.

beats.speaker: Dee
beats.text: Room’s half college kids, half ranchers. Read the room.

choices.label: “I’m in. See you at 8.”
“What’s the cash-to-beer ratio?”

beats.speaker: Dee
beats.text: Sixty bucks and a growler.

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: That’s more than my last three gigs combined.

beats.speaker: Dee
beats.text: That’s sad. See you at 8.

brewery.title: Read the room
brewery.artDesc: A warm Ellensburg brewery taproom with a tiny stage: college students in hoodies at one table, ranchers in work jackets and cowboy hats at another. Dee, behind the bar, points Brendan to the stage.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: Half the room is college kids. The other half came in from a ranch and has opinions.

beats.speaker: Dee
beats.text: Don’t play anything sad before nine.

beats.speaker: Rancher
beats.text: You know any real songs?

choices.label: Open with the jingle.
Open with a classic everyone knows.
Open with the new song.

openJingle.title: Common ground
openJingle.artDesc: On stage, Brendan grins as the whole taproom sings: a college kid and a big rancher clink glasses mid-chorus.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: The college kids know it from their childhood. The ranchers know it from the radio. For one chorus, Ellensburg is united.

beats.speaker: Rancher
beats.text: Dang it. That’s been stuck in my head since my divorce.

openCover.title: A real song
openCover.artDesc: Brendan on stage, eyes closed, playing an old classic; ranchers nod along, a rancher tips his hat.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: He plays an old song everyone’s dad loved. The ranchers nod. A college kid asks who wrote it.

beats.speaker: Rancher
beats.text: Now that’s a real song.

openNew.title: Before nine
openNew.artDesc: Brendan on stage mid-song; the clock above the bar reads 8:52. Dee shoots him a warning look; the room has gone quiet and listening.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: It’s sad, and it’s 8:52. Dee gives him a look. The room goes quiet anyway, the good kind of quiet.

beats.speaker: Dee
beats.text: Eight minutes early. I’ll allow it.

video.title: Someone posted it
video.artDesc: Late night: Brendan’s phone blowing up with the crew’s group chat; a shared video thumbnail shows him on the brewery stage.

beats.speaker: Scene
beats.text: A student posts a video of the set. By midnight it has more views than Ellensburg has people.

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Is this you?? In ELLENSBURG??

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: Please tell me nobody there knows where the reunion is.

beats.speaker: Dan
beats.text: He’s an Ellensburg celebrity now. Ellensburg.

beats.speaker: Jay
beats.text: The shirt is working. I’d like credit.

choices.label: “Your secret’s safe. Probably.”
“Opening act. They want me back.”

safe.title: Probably

beats.speaker: Andrew
beats.text: PROBABLY??

beats.speaker: Brendan
beats.text: It’s my favorite kind.

safe.end: Sixty dollars, a growler, and a video he hasn’t watched yet. Next stop: Vantage.

flex.title: They want him back

beats.speaker: Dee
beats.text: Same time next month? Bring the guy with the keyboard.

beats.speaker: Dan
beats.text: Okay, that’s actually cool. I hate it.

flex.end: Sixty dollars, a growler, and a second booking. Next stop: Vantage.
